title: Futex PI cycle detection and nested donation cleanup
summary: Close the next Linux rt_mutex compatibility gaps after priority-ordered handoff: explicit PI owner-chain deadlock detection and nested donation deboost after timeout/cancel.

write_sets.notes: Single-agent futex PI slice in codex/futex-linux-compat worktree.

steps.title: Pin direct owner-chain cycle detection with EDEADLK
steps.notes: Add a red test with two live threads: A owns futex_a, B owns futex_b, B blocks on futex_a, then A attempts FUTEX_LOCK_PI on futex_b. Expected result is -EDEADLK and no new waiter/donation row for A. This mirrors Linux rt_mutex full chain walk returning -EDEADLK when the blocking task appears again in the owner chain.

steps.title: Add futex-side chain walk helper before enqueue/requeue mutation
steps.notes: Introduce a helper shaped like pi_chain_would_deadlock(waiter_tid, owner_tid) -> Result<(), Errno>. Walk existing FutexPiWaiter rows by waiter_tid -> blocked_owner_tid up to FUTEX_PI_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH. Return EDEADLK if the walk reaches waiter_tid again or exceeds the bound; return ESRCH if a nonzero owner in the chain is no longer live. Call it after owner self-check/ESRCH validation but before inserting a new PI waiter or moving WAIT_REQUEUE_PI rows to PI_WAITERS.

steps.title: Pin CMP_REQUEUE_PI cycle detection without source-row loss
steps.notes: Add a red test where a WAIT_REQUEUE_PI waiter would be requeued to a PI target whose owner is already blocked on a PI futex owned by that waiter. Expected CMP_REQUEUE_PI returns -EDEADLK, leaves the waiter on the source futex, and a later FUTEX_WAKE on the source resumes it with -EAGAIN.

steps.title: Apply chain walk to requeue before removing source waiters
steps.notes: In step_futex_cmp_requeue_pi_in, do the source wait-kind validation and target owner read first, run the chain walk for each selected requeue waiter against the target owner, and only then remove source rows. Keep the current ESRCH preservation property intact.

steps.title: Pin nested timeout/cancel deboost for direct LOCK_PI
steps.notes: Add focused tests for A<-B<-C where C has high RT priority and blocks on B while B blocks on A. Abort C's FutexPiLockOp through immediate zero-timeout or explicit cancellation path already available in the dispatch/StepOp harness. Expected: C row removed, B returns to base/effective priority without C, and A loses the propagated donation from B if no other higher donor remains.

steps.title: Recompute owner-chain donations after PI waiter removal
steps.notes: Extend step_futex_pi_cancel_wait_source and any timeout/cancel cleanup path to remember the blocked_owner_tid whose donation was removed. After dropping the token and row, recompute remaining direct donations for that owner, then call propagate_pi_donation_from(owner_tid) or a new recompute_pi_chain_from(owner_tid) to push deboost/down-propagation upward. The helper must handle no remaining donors by leaving effective priority at the scheduler base value.

steps.title: Pin nested timeout/cancel deboost for WAIT_REQUEUE_PI after target requeue
steps.notes: Add coverage for a WAIT_REQUEUE_PI waiter moved to a contended target PI futex, then timing out/canceling while behind a target owner that is itself blocked on another PI futex. Expected cleanup removes the target PI waiter row, drops the target-owner donation, and down-propagates the loss to the upstream owner.

steps.title: Run full focused verification and progress catch-up
steps.notes: Update STATUS.md and the PI readiness research note with what changed, verification, remaining Linux gaps, and any blocker. Keep the plan status proposed unless all steps are completed in the implementation run.

verification.notes: 30 futex-filtered tx-subsystems tests passed after implementation.
cargo -q xtask unit passed after implementation.

risks: Current donation tokens are edge-local but the scheduler API lacks an explicit donor-owner-futex reason key; recompute helpers must avoid leaking duplicate donations.
Cycle detection must run before mutating source/requeue wait rows or error paths will lose waiters.
Down-propagation on deboost is more subtle than upward donation: removing a top donor may reveal a lower donor that still needs to propagate.
Linux rt_mutex uses priority trees and task pi_waiters; this plan intentionally keeps the current vector table and closes observable semantics first.
